name: Hoac Foods India Limited
sector: Branded staples, food processing and regional distribution
summary: Rapid regional staples growth is real in reported sales, but multi-year negative cash conversion, restricted QIP funding and an expensive entry multiple weaken shareholder economics. Conditional funded base IRR−6.88%, bull11.07%; no-rescue survival requires disciplined procurement and existing WC renewal. Large lots impair implementation.
identity_note: Annual report, prospectus and eligible 19 October ST security-master row agree on HOACFOODS and the ISIN. Issued shares: 4,340,460; lot size: 375.

quote.kind: official close; not a live executable quote

score_note: Canonical v3.0 exact weights. Persistent CASH 3 caps GQS at 5. IAS is conditional on the ₹5 lakh reference and funded phasing assumptions. Displays: 5.3 / 5.0 / 2.6.

gates.reason: No substantiated abuse or disqualifying integrity event established in reviewed primary disclosures. Promoter control and intercompany funding require continued scrutiny; audit findings are scoped assurance, not proof of absence.

Signed group faces reconcile. Some detailed notes use parent figures, historical original/restated FY2023 amounts differ, and QIP expense classifications differ by ₹0.098 crore. Scope-specific bridges avoid mixing these figures; conservative credit exclusions and sensitivities bound the model impact. This is not treated as missing cash or fraud.

Flat ₹50 crore revenue, a 10% margin and prior 116-day debtor collection survive without rescue when inventory is reduced to 85 sales-days and discretionary expansion is deferred. Keeping 100 inventory days under the same collection stress creates a ₹1.10 crore gap. Seasonal procurement supports a management response, but facility renewal and actual execution remain unverified. Hypothetical new capital is not used to pass this gate.

Actual 19 October trades and an eligible ST series support listed tradability, not suspension. The ₹3.72 lakh lot, thin trade counts and next-session ESM Stage I prevent assuming executable ₹5 lakh capacity. No live bid/ask test was available.

sections.title: 1. Executive verdict
sections.text:
Hoac is a fast-growing regional staples business, but business growth and shareholder return are not interchangeable. FY2026 consolidated revenue rose 89.3% to ₹50.11 crore and owner profit reached ₹4.41 crore. Operating cash flow was negative ₹4.22 crore, mainly because inventory absorbed ₹9.73 crore. That is not capex: another ₹2.70 crore of cash was invested in fixed assets and CWIP. ₹5.10 crore of March cash was unused QIP money earmarked for working capital, leaving ₹1.43 crore initially unrestricted. [S1,S7]

At the verified ₹991.85 close, market capitalization is ₹430.51 crore and the trailing owner-earnings multiple is about 73.2×. The claim-inclusive, conditionally funded base case produces −6.9% annualized over five years; the bull case produces 11.1%, still below the 15% research hurdle. Strong operating progress is therefore insufficient on its own to justify this entry price. The important counterargument is that distribution and capacity expansion could sustain exceptional growth for longer; it still requires cash and an unusually durable valuation premium.

Final BQS 5.26, GQS 5.00 after the cash-conversion cap, and IAS 2.565. Classification: weak setup / value-trap risk at the observed price, not a finding of fraudulent conduct or inevitable insolvency. A large minimum lot and concentrated trading further limit implementation. The ₹5 lakh reference is illustrative, not a proposed allocation.

sections.title: 2. Scope, dates and comparability
sections.text:
Hoac Foods India Limited; NSE SME HOACFOODS; ISIN INE0S6S01017. Research cutoff: 20 October 2026. Last observed market session: 19 October 2026. Accounts follow the Indian accounting standards applicable to this issuer, with figures converted to ₹ crore. FY2021–23 uses visually checked restated prospectus tables; FY2024 original parent accounts are a separate version; FY2025–26 group faces supply the latest comparative basis. Parent sales endpoints are preferred for long-window growth because HOAC Exports, owned 75%, and Rajdhara Foods, owned 51%, joined the group in January 2025 and February 2026. These are new controlled operating entities, not evidence of a large acquired revenue book. [S1–S5]

The FY2023 original annual-report comparison showed different profit and cash-flow amounts from the IPO restatement. These versions are disclosed, not silently blended. Some FY2026 detailed notes reproduce parent amounts while the signed consolidated faces differ; the model uses group faces and explicitly reconciles component residuals. This is bounded scope uncertainty, not a claim that cash is missing. Historical-input confidence is Medium overall; forecast uncertainty is High. October cash cannot be inferred merely from the June profit statement.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and gates
sections.text:
BQS combines GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 3, BAL 5 and EXEC 6 using the canonical 20/20/12/10/12/10/8/8 weights, yielding 5.26. GQS combines REV 8, DUR 6, EARN 7, CAP 6 and CASH 3 at 40/20/15/15/10, yielding raw 6.65, capped at 5 because poor cash realization is multi-year rather than a single inventory quarter. IAS uses final BQS 5.26, R 1, D 2, P 2 and L 3 at 25/35/20/10/10, yielding 2.565. Half-up one-decimal displays are 5.3, 5.0 and 2.6. No missing factor was filled with a neutral 5; every factor has an evidence-linked reason.

G1 Integrity, G2 Accounting reliability, G3 Stress survival and G4 Tradability are conditional, not automatic failures. Reviewed audits do not establish abuse. Accounting versions and component limitations can be bounded without inventing precision. Essential-operation stress has a source-supported, no-rescue inventory response, whereas discretionary growth and facility nonrenewal variants can fail. Actual trades support tradability but not dependable lot execution. Scores remain conditional on these facts and the ₹5 lakh reference. Confidence labels are not raised merely to preserve high scores.

sections.title: 4. Business, industry and economic model
sections.text:
Hoac manufactures, processes and trades atta, pulses, spices, oils and related staples under Hariom. Own stores, franchise stores, general-trade/B2B customers and export channels have different economics. Management described FY2026 revenue mix of 21.83%, 18.65%, 52.34% and 7.18%, respectively. This is therefore not simply a high-margin direct-to-consumer brand. B2B expansion increases reach but can require trade credit and lower per-unit margins. Raw-material procurement and product handling consume working capital before receipts arrive. [S1,S6]

The October update described 23+ outlets, 235+ SKUs, reach into 4,000+ kiranas and approximately 1.2 lakh consumers, plus exports. These are management reach indicators, not audited same-store sales or repeat-order cohorts. The Bhopal opening outside Delhi-NCR and an additional Gurugram franchise provide geographic tests; profitable replication is not yet established. Milling and processing capacity, product quality and local routes can support growth, but commodity prices, food safety, procurement seasonality and distributor credit remain central risks. This is an operating consumer-staples and manufacturing/distribution business, not a lender requiring an NBFC valuation adaptation.

sections.title: 5. Moat and peer context
sections.text:
Local familiarity, freshness, assortment and route density may lower customer acquisition costs in the existing catchment. None alone demonstrates a durable moat. The prospectus describes competitive suppliers and fragmented staples markets rather than exclusive inputs or contractual customer lock-in. Current consumer retention, price realization versus comparable products and cohort contribution margins are not disclosed well enough to prove pricing power. MOAT 4 recognizes operating and franchise know-how while refusing to capitalize regional brand claims as a national franchise. [S4,S6,S8]

Megastar Foods reports 710 MTPD processing capacity and industrial customers, illustrating scale and quality capabilities outside Hoac. Sarveshwar has rice/organic integration and branded retail, including 15 stores and seven NIMBARK organic stores. ITC combines branded foods with nationwide sourcing, product development and distribution. These are competitive capabilities, not inputs to a peer-multiple average: product mixes, capital structures and channels differ substantially. Hoac can win locally without matching these firms, but evidence does not support national brand rents, supplier leverage or enduring high margins at many times its current scale. [S13–S15]

sections.title: 6. Revenue growth: magnitude and source
sections.text:
Restated parent revenue was ₹7.42 crore in FY2021, ₹10.87 crore in FY2022 and ₹12.09 crore in FY2023. FY2024 parent sales were ₹15.63 crore, the latest FY2025 comparison was ₹26.48 crore, and FY2026 parent sales were ₹48.75 crore; group revenue was ₹50.11 crore. Parent five-year CAGR is 45.7%; the three-year endpoint CAGR is 59.2%. Using parent endpoints avoids treating all subsidiary sales as comparable organic growth. The IPO prospectus also describes channel reclassification involving Farm2Home, so channel rows are not a constant-perimeter, same-store series. [S1–S4]

June 2026 quarterly group sales of ₹20.05 crore versus ₹8.42 crore indicate continued rapid expansion, but one quarter is not a full-year run rate and no matching cash-flow statement was supplied. October's H1 update adds distribution evidence, not audited H1 revenue. Volume, realized price, new-store contribution, existing-store growth and intercompany elimination effects are not separately quantified at decision-grade quality. Revenue growth starts high under the numerical rubric, but REV is capped at 8 for Medium comparability and decomposition confidence. Small absolute size alone is not the reason for the cap. [S5,S8]

sections.title: 7. Durability, earnings quality and incremental returns
sections.text:
Staple consumption provides a durable demand category, not a durable right to each customer's spending. New kirana access and more outlets are plausible growth channels; their returns depend on collections, discounts, utilization and repeat purchases. Management's proposed 45–50 TPD from 20 TPD is a numerical 2.25–2.5× capacity step, not the inconsistent verbal 5× claim. The proposed ₹4.5–5 crore expansion was described as using a mix of borrowing and own resources. No independent commissioning certificate was retrieved. The base assumes capacity and reinvestment support ₹174 crore terminal annual sales; the ₹272 crore bull requires additional funded investment, not free capacity. [S6]

FY2026 operating EBITDA, recomputed as PBT plus interest and depreciation minus other income, was ₹6.93 crore. Other income of ₹0.38 crore is not treated as operating growth. June quarterly operating EBITDA is ₹3.09 crore. Owner profits and operating margins support EARN 7, but issued shares increased from 3.843 million to 4.340 million after the July 2025 QIP, so profit growth cannot substitute for per-share growth. [S1,S5]

The financing-side invested-capital proxy, equity plus debt minus all cash, rises from ₹3.14 crore in FY2023 to ₹24.68 crore in FY2026. With normalized 25% tax on operating EBIT, three-year incremental return is approximately 19.1% and five-year return 19.4%. This is a diagnostic, not audited ROIC: it excludes tax and legacy-claim adjustments and crosses a small subsidiary-perimeter change. Full opening operating capital, including PPE, intangibles, CWIP, deposits and ordinary working capital, is ₹26.01 crore; incremental economics are less impressive on that basis. CAP 6 reflects mixed confidence against an assumed 14–18% capital-cost range, not a claimed live WACC. New cohorts and the factory lack a full-cycle cash-return record.

sections.title: 8. Governance, capital allocation and related parties
sections.text:
March 2026 promoter ownership was 62.08%. IPO shares in May 2024 and 497,250 QIP shares at ₹201 in July 2025 enlarged outside capital; issued shares, not weighted-average EPS shares, determine current market value. No additional warrant or ESOP overhang was identified in the reviewed capital disclosures and subsequent-announcement scope, but this is not a guarantee against undiscovered instruments. The latest detailed pledge position was not independently established. [S1,S2,S4,S10]

The parent funds and trades with controlled subsidiaries. Its ₹1.70 crore advance to HOAC Exports is eliminated in consolidated analysis, not counted as cash recoverable from an independent party. The FY2027 ₹44 crore proposed RPT ceiling combines ₹12 crore sales, ₹4 crore purchases, ₹15 crore loans/advances and ₹13 crore repayments; describing the whole ceiling as new exposure would be misleading. Shareholder and audit-committee approvals and disclosed arm's-length assertions are safeguards, not independent proof of economic fairness. Settlement, margins and minority leakage merit scrutiny; gross turnover alone does not establish wrongdoing. [S1]

Reviewed opinions are unmodified, with scoped CARO findings of no borrowing default and no fraud noticed or reported. These do not justify either an unconditional clean bill of health or an allegation of abuse. Director remuneration and governance arrangements do not themselves explain weak cash realization. GOV 5 balances the findings against concentrated control, financing dependence and limited independent evidence on related-party pricing.

sections.title: 9. Financial forensics and claim audit
sections.text:
FY2026 group PAT of ₹4.41 crore versus CFO of −₹4.22 crore is the principal forensic divergence. Inventory increased ₹9.73 crore while receivables released ₹0.44 crore; procurement, not debtor deterioration alone, drove the latest drain. Cash capex of ₹2.70 crore then made CFO less capex −₹6.92 crore, before interest classified in financing. Three-year FY2024–26 CFO/PAT is −72.1%; earlier restated FY2021–23 cash generation was also weak. This supports persistent CASH 3 and the GQS cap despite management's seasonality and distribution explanations. It does not establish fictitious sales. [S1–S4,S6]

The opening consolidated balance sheet balances at ₹35.57 crore. Ordinary working capital is ₹19.70 crore: receivables ₹8.01 plus inventory ₹13.60 plus other operating assets ₹0.81, less trade payables ₹1.89 and other current liabilities ₹0.82. Statutory, employee/expense and customer-advance components remain within these liabilities. Current income tax of ₹1.5075 crore is explicitly paid in the first six modeled months. Current gratuity of ₹0.0102 crore and noncurrent gratuity of ₹0.0563 crore are separately scheduled; future employee costs remain in EBITDA. Deferred tax of ₹0.0589 crore survives as a terminal claim. [S1]

The ₹0.0786 crore tax-authority credit receives no base recovery because eligibility and timing are unverified; it is not credited through working capital as well. A ₹0.2232 crore doubtful advance is excluded from recoverable value without a fictional cash release. Interest receivable of ₹0.0083 crore is a one-time assumed June receipt. Deposits remain operating assets. Intercompany balances are eliminated and group residuals explicitly included. These are model treatments, not new company restatements.

Group cash of ₹6.5324 crore splits into ₹5.10 crore earmarked QIP funds and ₹1.4324 crore unrestricted. Certified deployment was ₹2 crore through June; later release is only against authorized gross working-capital costs. Proceeds are never added again at exit. A ₹0.0976 crore difference between issue-expense presentations is tested as an additional-payment sensitivity, not asserted to be unpaid. Reviewed notes did not identify an additional material acquisition payment, dividend payable or omitted capital creditor; ordinary expenses remain in working capital. Model interest of 14–15% deliberately exceeds the cheapest secured loans because disclosed borrowing costs also include expensive unsecured facilities. [S1,S5,S7]

sections.title: 10. Valuation and five-year funded return model
sections.text:
At ₹991.85 on 19 October, 4,340,460 shares imply ₹430.51 crore equity value. Adding ₹6.10 crore debt and subtracting only ₹1.43 crore initial unrestricted cash gives conservative EV of ₹435.17 crore. Trailing June revenue of ₹61.74 crore, owner PAT of ₹5.88 crore and operating EBITDA of ₹9.07 crore imply approximately 73.2× PE and 48.0× EV/EBITDA. These are scope-correct calculations, not undated intake ratios. [S1,S5,S9,S10]

The model starts from audited March balances, incorporates observed June quarterly P&L, then estimates monthly cash, debt and claims through 19 October 2031. Investor returns begin on 19 October 2026; pre-entry estimated cash remains part of the bridge. Monthly allocations and post-March cash balances are assumptions. The FY2032 terminal annual run rate determines EV, but only cash generated through 19 October is added. No dividends, new borrowing or equity issuance occur in the main cases.

Bear: FY2027 sales of ₹60 crore, subsequent growth of 5–6%, terminal sales ₹78.79 crore; margin 10.5% recovering to 12%; 85 debtor and 80 inventory sales-days; ₹1 crore first-year capex and 2.5% of sales thereafter; 8× exit EBITDA. The conditional funded terminal price is ₹184.20 and IRR −28.59%.

Base: FY2027 sales of ₹75 crore, then growth of 25%, 22%, 18%, 15% and 12%, reaching ₹173.83 crore; margin 14.5%; 60 debtor and 75 inventory days; ₹4.5 crore first-year capex and 3.5% thereafter; 12× exit. Terminal EV of ₹302.47 crore plus cash ₹12.13 crore, less debt ₹3.80 crore, legacy claims ₹0.06 crore and NCI ₹9.32 crore, produces common equity of ₹301.41 crore, ₹694.43 per share and IRR −6.88%.

Bull: FY2027 sales of ₹90 crore, then growth of 35%, 30%, 25%, 20% and 15%, reaching ₹272.46 crore; margin 16–17%; 50 debtor and 65 inventory days; ₹5 crore first-year capex and 5% thereafter; 16× exit. Conditional funded terminal price is ₹1,676.53 and IRR 11.07%. An 18× terminal PAT crosscheck yields lower base and bull prices of ₹658.19 and ₹1,211.90. That is a separate earnings normalization, not a second cash addition.

Current term maturities of ₹0.568 crore are paid monthly in FY2027, remaining term debt of ₹1.73 crore over the following 48 months; existing working-capital debt of ₹3.80 crore is retained with renewal assumed. Taxes are 27% of positive pretax income plus separately paid legacy tax. The base FY2027 bridge is opening unrestricted cash ₹1.4324 plus operating cash after interest, tax and working capital ₹2.1964, less capex ₹4.50, term repayment ₹0.5679, legacy tax ₹1.5075 and legacy benefits ₹0.0215, plus earmarked release ₹5.10 and interest recovery ₹0.0083, equaling ₹2.1402 crore. No omitted claim or imaginary facility funds it.

Sensitivity grids vary growth from 10–30%, exit multiples from 8–16×, margins from 10–16%, inventory from 55–115 days and terminal minority claims from 1–10%. Unfunded variants receive no IRR. Front-loaded plant payments create a ₹0.1285 crore temporary gap despite unchanged annual spending, so the base requires feasible phasing, not merely positive year-end cash. Its 15% hurdle-entry diagnostic is about ₹345, not a guaranteed fair value or instruction to buy. Forecast uncertainty remains High.

sections.title: 11. Bear case and no-rescue survival
sections.text:
Stress follows observed risks rather than stacking an industry collapse, asset wipeout and complete financing withdrawal. A restrained no-rescue case holds sales near ₹50 crore, reduces the margin to 10%, postpones expansion to ₹0.6 crore essential spending and models 88 debtor/100 inventory days. It survives on existing cash, authorized QIP working capital and existing facility renewal, without new capital. Business survival does not protect the current price: terminal share value is approximately ₹131, a severe permanent-loss path.

FY2025 receivables were about 116 sales-days. Reverting to 116 days while keeping 100 inventory days under flat revenue and a 10% margin produces a ₹1.10 crore cumulative gap, with no IRR assigned. But inventory is a procurement decision: reducing it to 85 sales-days, consistent with avoiding the large seasonal stock build, funds the same collection stress with minimum cash of about ₹0.95 crore. Lower procurement benefits are not free; the 10% margin already allows less favorable input economics. No inventory write-off is layered on top of the same cash release. [S1,S6]

This countercase supports Conditional G3 rather than an automatic Fail. If lenders refuse existing working-capital renewal, the restrained case develops a ₹0.86 crore gap; that is a financing boundary, not evidence of an actual call or default. Hypothetical rescue equity and debt are modeled separately with fees, dilution and same-period interest, never to prove no-rescue survival. Supplier credit, stock quality and legal cash access can change the result. Actual post-June evidence is needed. Severe current-price losses support D 2 even without insolvency.

sections.title: 12. Multibagger and reverse-expectations test
sections.text:
A stock already capitalizing rapid growth does not become attractive merely because revenue can multiply. The 15% five-year hurdle requires ₹865.82 crore terminal common equity, approximately twice today's market value. On the base operating path that requires 35.1× terminal EBITDA rather than 12×. Holding base cash, debt and minority assumptions constant, a 12× multiple and 14.5% margin require approximately ₹508 crore annual sales. That algebra is not a funded business plan: additional inventory, receivables, capacity and minority economics would change.

The constant-growth grid of 10–70% after FY2027 finds no fully self-funded 12× exit path meeting 15% under the model's capital needs. Faster growth can increase terminal accounting value while creating an earlier cash shortfall; those paths are not scored as returns. The bull delivers only about 1.69× terminal share value and 11.1% annualized even with ₹272 crore sales and a 17% margin. A doubling is not impossible, but the burden is sustained outperformance or a very rich remaining multiple, not an overlooked cheap base. P 2 expresses demanding price-implied expectations, not a prediction of the exact future quote.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring and decision triggers
sections.text:
Evidence that would upgrade the thesis: signed H1 or full-year cash flows showing positive conversion after ordinary taxes and interest; falling inventory days without write-offs or quality loss; sustained collections with controlled trade credit; verified commissioning and paid capex; profitable repeated outlet cohorts; and clearer group note disclosures. More promised capacity or distribution reach alone is insufficient.

Downgrade triggers: persistent negative CFO even when growth slows; aged receivables or obsolete inventory; overdue legacy tax or benefit obligations; facility nonrenewal; expensive dilution; subsidiary advances rising without settlement; or inability to execute even one lot at a reasonable spread. Each needs fresh primary evidence, not inference from a surveillance flag.

One 375-share lot costs ₹371,943.75; two lots cost ₹743,887.50, exceeding the illustrative ₹5 lakh reference. Sixty sessions contain 58 observations and two unknown absences. Conditional zero-filled mean/median turnover is ₹29.86/24.34 lakh, implying 4.11, 10.27 and 2.05 theoretical exit days at 5%, 2% and 10% participation. Observed-only statistics are retained separately. Latest 20-session mean/median is ₹22.13/17.92 lakh, giving 5.58 days at 5%. Only three of 58 observed sessions, and none of the latest 20, can fit one current-price lot within a 5% turnover allowance. Thus L starts at 7 from the longer formula but falls to 3 for lot granularity and concentrated trading. Live depth is unknown. ESM Stage I and cautions in the 19 October EOD file apply on 21 October, not retroactively on 19 October. No automation or trade has been created. [S9–S12,S17]

sections.title: 14. Classification and what would change the view
sections.text:
Weak setup / value-trap risk at the observed price. The label describes the gap between strong growth and weak cash/valuation support; it does not imply a low-multiple trap, misconduct or actual default. Business quality is mid-range, growth quality is cash-capped and investment attractiveness is low. This is not a verified long-duration compounder or low-risk multibagger candidate.

A much lower entry price, materially better funded economics or a convincing reason for a durable high terminal multiple would improve valuation. Better cash conversion and mature incremental returns would independently improve business and growth scores. An unfunded optional expansion does not force G3 Fail when essential operations can be curtailed to survive; demonstrated inability to settle existing claims under credible, controllable stress would. Ranking eligibility remains conditional on Medium input confidence, the observed price and illustrative liquidity size. The 15% hurdle is a nominal, pre-personal-tax INR equity return, not a personal required-return assessment.

sections.title: 15. Sources, assumptions and unresolved questions
sections.text:
Audited annual reports, the restated prospectus, signed June results, QIP certificates and dated exchange files anchor the analysis. Management calls and operating updates are identified as M, calculations as C and forward assumptions as A. Source IDs, exact URLs and reviewed locators are supplied. Primary peer materials inform competitive context, not automatic valuation. The 15% hurdle, 14–18% capital-cost range, future growth, margins, multiples, working-capital targets, capex phasing, claim settlement schedules and minority value fractions are analyst assumptions, not issuer facts.

Important gaps remain: actual October funding; post-March capex dates; renewal terms; current pledge detail; customer/supplier concentration; price/volume decomposition; outlet unit returns; tax-credit eligibility; subsidiary cash-transfer restrictions; and executable live depth. They are bounded where possible by financing cases, conservative exclusions and sensitivities, not filled with invented data. Historical version differences, parent/group presentation and QIP fee reconciliation remain explicit. Some historical KPI EBITDA labels do not reconcile with the restated P&L, so operating EBITDA is recomputed from PBT, interest, depreciation and other income. These analytical cautions are not allegations of accounting fraud. New evidence can change scores and valuation.

Group financial faces reconcile but several detailed note amounts reproduce parent figures. Residual group assets/liabilities are explicitly allocated; future subsidiary cash access and minority economics remain uncertain.
FY2023 restated prospectus and later original comparator differ. Historical versions are kept separate, and comparable FY2024–26 cash weakness carries the conclusion.
Current pledge detail, top customer/supplier concentration, audited segment economics, price-volume growth and mature outlet cohort returns are not established.
Capacity commissioning and exact capex payment dates are unverified. Frontloading optional capex creates a small funding gap; no IRR is assigned to that unfunded variant.
Working-capital facility renewal is assumed for surviving cases, not newly committed financing. Restricted QIPcash can be used only for approvedobjects.
NCI terminal3–4%share is a scenario approximation across two differently owned subsidiaries;1–10%sensitivity is provided. No precise subsidiary DCF is claimed.
Live spreads, depth and circuit exits are not observed. Two absent historical sessions are unknown; zero filling is conditional, not a finding of zero trades.
No independent peer-normalized valuation set or fully reviewed current credit-rating rationale is used. Multiples and14–18%costofcapitalrange are analyst assumptions, not verified marketWACC.
Model outcomes and scores are research conventions, not personalized advice, trade recommendations or empirically validated return probabilities.

Recheck current issued shares, pledge pattern and live lot/depth before an implementation decision.

GOV.reason: Unmodified audit and disclosed RPT terms support a mixed, not disqualifying governance assessment. Promoter control, substantial intercompany funding and unverified latest pledge detail constrain assurance. No evidence of abuse is inferred from RPT size.

MOAT.reason: Regional brand and route density provide some customer convenience, but branded staples face local mills and much larger networks. Repeat purchasing, pricing power and defensible outlet returns are not established.

REV.reason: Parent five-year revenue CAGR exceeds the top raw growth band, but channel/perimeter comparability and unobserved price-volume decomposition give Medium confidence and cap the score at 8.

DUR.reason: Recurring staples demand, additional outlets and wider kirana distribution create a plausible runway. Geographic expansion and a lower-margin B2B mix still require capital and proven repeat demand.

CAP.reason: Incremental capital-return proxies near19% are above an assumed14–18% capital-cost range, but not decisively above its upper end after a full operating-capital reconciliation. New capacity/store cohorts lack mature cash returns.

CASH.reason: FY2024–26 cumulative CFO/PAT is negative, following weak earlier restated cash realization. FY2026 inventory explains much of the latest absorption, but repeated external capital dependence is not a single transitory quarter.

BAL.reason: Equity and earmarked QIP money support authorized working capital, while term amortization and legacy taxes are payable. Only₹1.43 crore March cash is initially unrestricted; renewal and procurement discipline matter.

EXEC.reason: Sales/distribution and quarterly operating profits show execution. Independently verified capacity commissioning, mature store productivity and post-June cash conversion remain absent.

EARN.reason: Growth is mainly operating, with other income only a small portion of FY2026 PBT and continuing June-quarter profit growth. QIP dilution and mix changes temper per-share quality; weak cash conversion is scored separately.

R.reason: Conditional funded base IRR−6.88% minus 15% hurdle is−21.88 percentage points, below −10; canonical R=1.

D.reason: Bear terminal equity value implies roughly81% loss at the current entry even when operations remain funded; optional expansion and prior debtor-day stresses add financing sensitivity.

P.reason: Earning15% requires about35.1× terminal EBITDA on the base operating path, or much faster capital-intensive growth. Even a17% margin/16×exit bull case yields only11.1%.

L.reason: The conditional60-day formula starts at7, but a₹3.72 lakh lot cannot fit a5%daily participation budget in any recent20session. ESM and concentrated trading further weaken implementation; live depth is unverified.
